verdict: Finite model supports full-history retention, dependency-safe GC and excision, but safe asynchronous destruction needs a complete ownership census, durable disposal identities and cross-repository publication fencing.
evidence_type: Executed deterministic Python simulations using synthetic local files; no DML or OpenTofu integration.
counterexamples: Snapshot-only scanning deletes historically retained infrastructure.
Publication after GC approval/revalidation creates a stale-plan deletion race.
Deleting the sole cleanup identity strands pending adoption/disposal.
Key-only excision breaks retained artifacts; tombstones alone do not erase controlled copies.
Configuration regeneration does not recover lost operational state/address mapping.
global_coordination: Repository/export membership and resource-reference publication versus destruction
Durable cleanup identity handoff before research history disposal
safe_eventual_reconciliation: Configuration generation, adoption and cleanup retries only while durable identities/prerequisites remain protected; not destructive application from stale root summaries.
limitations: Fences and journal are in-memory, not crash-safe or distributed.
Incomplete dependencies or never-registered repositories are outside invariant coverage.
Erasure covers synthetic controlled copies only; an uncontrolled copy intentionally survives.
Configuration is a mapping view, not HCL; provider state/import/replacement behavior is untested.
next_experiment: Two local publisher processes plus a durable journal; kill deletion between reservation and unlink, then test publication rejection and cleanup restart.
